analysis.title: GS Garrett - weekend prep ... 4 Oct 2026
key_insights: The desk argues SPX spot no longer acts as the clearing price for risk. Correlations across most assets have broken down versus the S&P 500, which is increasingly correlated mostly with itself.

Bonds, rates, oil and consumer sentiment (at all-time lows) are each signalling something different from equities, while SPX implied vol sits in the low double digits. The desk says participants are waiting for a correlation-1 event to restore the old relationships, but such a 4+ sigma event is by definition infrequent.

Index returns are driven by a narrow set of forces, described as 'AI vs non-AI'. SPX moves in roughly 20bp increments and VIX is at levels normally seen in December. The credit and rates desks continue to signal high anxiety.

Barron's cover story this weekend calls the market 'scary' and divided, citing maximum dispersion and low breadth. The Stock Trader's Almanac suggests this is not a harbinger of immediate losses, but the desk's conversations and net positioning point the other way.
Earnings concentration: the top 10 contributing stocks are expected to account for over two-thirds of aggregate S&P 500 earnings growth this season.

Vanilla hedging advice: broaden beyond 'cheap SPX' puts. The desk traded a lot of IWM downside, HYG and TLT convexity, and single stock protection (upside and downside) last week. If a K-shaped economy turns into a K-shaped market, wing downside in SPX ex-AI is worth a look. The March 85% put costs 132bps versus 1.01% for SPX, and the March 80% put costs 93bps versus 0.71%.

Russell 2000 futures short exposure is extreme, so an aggressive move lower in yields could create a squeeze. The desk offers a 3-month dual digital (IWM above 108% and 10y SOFR below 35bps) paying 10:1.

A second light exotic is SPX lower and crude lower, which trades in the 6th percentile on a 2-year lookback. Adding a USO lower contingency cheapens the embedded SPX digital: 3m SPX below 96% and USO below 90% costs 6.1% for a 16:1 payout.

The desk promotes a weekly 'tail book' one-pager that backtests the payoff multiple on 3m 50, 25 and 10 delta options across the largest 3-month risk-off episodes of the past 20 years versus today's option cost.

Prime book: net leverage for fundamental long/short funds fell three weeks in a row to the lowest since liberation day and is near a 5-year low. Gross exposure is high, so the desk says low net should not be read as complacency.
Hedge funds rotated into TMT stocks in September while basically every other sector was net sold. The AI/TMT momentum trade is attracting more participants.

One-delta desk: NDX made a new all-time high this week and the cash desk finished the week balanced. Long-only demand returned in semiconductors, with MU (earnings) and NVDA (buyback) the two highlights. Turnover is quiet for this part of the calendar.

Futures: the desk recommended and traded IWM downside as the most convex hedge to a Q4 financial conditions scenario. CTAs and the futures market are already positioned, with R2K futures deeply depressed.

Derivatives: FICC ETF option volume has more than doubled over the last three weeks as traders use liquid ETF options to express macro views while indices decouple. The desk likes owning NDX or QQQ upside, including knock-out calls and QQQ-over-IWM outperformance structures. The market-implied probability of QQQ +5% in a month is twice that of SPX.
Baskets: the desk flags its consumer inertia basket (GSXUSWCH) and single stock hedging suite, and likes upside in sector-neutral high-beta stocks (GSPUBETA) and the power basket (GSX1POW1).
